text.p: Management of Abitibi-Price Inc and Stone-Consolidated Corp expect the merger of the two companies to result in a C$115 million charge, according to a proxy circular on the proposed amalgamation.

"Management expects to incur a nonrecurring charge resulting from the amalgamation of approximately C$115 million after an income tax benefit of C$60 million. Management believes that this charge will be accrued primarily in the second quarter of 1997," the proxy said.
Shareholders of each company are to vote on the merger proposal at special meetings in Montreal and Toronto on May 29.
According to the proxy, and as previously disclosed, the merger will result in annual cost savings of C$100 million once all plans relating to various synergies are realized.

In addition, the companies expect that the merger will result in annual interest savings of about C$20 million initially, and those savings will decline relative to the terms of the companies' existing credit arrangements.

In the proxy, both Abitibi-Price and Stone-Consolidated said they expect a newsprint price increase of US$75 a metric ton originally planned for either February or March to be fully implemented during the second quarter.

The merged company plans to divest, in whole or in part, its office products distribution division, which serves North America, including Mexico and Western Europe, as it is considered a non-core business, the proxy said.
The proxy did not indicate what proceeds the merged companies expect to receive from the divestiture.

As previously announced, the companies' head office will be consolidated in Montreal. Similar combinations are planned for research centers, U.S. central sales offices and sales offices in London, England, the proxy said.

Abitibi-Consolidated has commitments on a C$2.2 billion credit facility, which will be used in part to repay new bridge financing facilities and other existing financing arrangements, the proxy said. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
